first: श्लोक — वर्णानामर्थसङ्घनां रसानां छन्दसामपि।
en: I bow to Saraswati and Ganesha, who give rise to letters, meanings, moods of feeling, metres and all that is auspicious.

first: भवानीशङ्करौ वन्दे श्रद्धाविश्वासरूपिणौ।
en: I bow to Bhavani and Shankar, who are faith and trust in bodily form; without them even the perfected ones cannot see the Lord who lives in their own hearts.

first: वन्दे बोधमयं नित्यं गुरुं, शङ्कररूपिणम्।
en: I bow to the Guru, who is all knowledge, eternal, and Shankar himself; resting on him, even the crooked moon is honoured everywhere.

first: सीतारामगुणग्रामपुण्यारण्यविहारिणौ।
en: I bow to the king of poets (Valmiki) and the king of monkeys (Hanuman), pure in wisdom, who roam the holy forest of the virtues of Sita and Rama.

first: उद्भवस्थितिसंहारकारिणीं क्लेशहारिणीम्।
en: I bow to Sita, Rama's beloved, who brings about creation, keeping and ending of the world, removes all pain and gives every good.

first: यन्मायावशवर्त्ति विश्वमखिलं ब्रह्मादिदेवासुराः।
en: I worship Hari, the Lord called Rama, beyond all causes; the whole world, with Brahma, gods and demons, is under his maya, and by his being this false world seems real, like a snake seen in a rope; his feet are the only boat for those who wish to cross the sea of birth.

first: नानापुराणनिगमागमसम्मतं यद्रामायणे निगदितं क्वचिदन्यतोऽपि।
en: For the joy of his own heart, Tulsi writes the story of Raghunath in the common tongue, very beautiful, in line with the Puranas, Vedas and scriptures, with what the Ramayana tells and some things from elsewhere.

first: सोरठा-जेहि सुमिरत सिधि होइ, गन-नायक करि-बर-बदन।
en: May Ganesha, leader of Shiva's hosts, with the fine face of an elephant, store of wisdom and home of good qualities, by remembering whom all aims succeed, show me his grace.

first: मूक होइ बाचाल, पङ्गु चढ़इ गिरिवर गहन।
en: May the kind one by whose grace the dumb speak well and the lame climb steep mountains, who burns away all the sins of the Kali age, melt with mercy for me.

first: नील-सरोरुह-स्याम, तरुन-अरुन-बारिज नयन।
en: May he who is dark like the blue lotus, with eyes like a fresh red lotus, who always lies on the ocean of milk, make his home in my heart.

first: कुन्द-इन्दु-सम देह, उमा-रमन करुना-अयन।
en: May Uma's lord, fair as the jasmine and the moon, home of mercy, who loves the humble and who burned the god of love, be kind to me.

first: बन्दउँ गुरु-पद-कञ्ज, कृपा-सिन्धु नर-रूप-हरि।
en: I bow to the lotus feet of my Guru, an ocean of mercy, Hari in human form, whose words are like the sun's rays that scatter the deep darkness of delusion.

first: चौ॰—बन्दउँ गुरु-पद-पदुम-परागा। सुरुचि-सुबास सरस अनुरागा॥
en: I bow to the dust of my Guru's lotus feet, fragrant with good taste and rich with love; it is a fine powder made of the herb of nectar that cures the whole family of worldly ills.

first: सुकृत सम्भू-तन विमल बिभूती। मज्जुल मङ्गल-मोद-प्रसूती॥
en: It is the pure holy ash on the body of Shiva-like merit, the mother of beauty, blessing and joy; it wipes the dirt from the bright mirror of the devotee's mind, and worn as a mark on the brow it wins all virtues.

first: श्रीगुरु-पद-नख मनि-गन-जोती। सुमिरत दिव्य-दृष्टि हिय होती।
en: The light of the gem-like nails of the Guru's feet gives the heart divine sight when one remembers it; it destroys the darkness of delusion, and lucky is the one in whose heart it shines.

first: उघरहिँ बिमल बिलोचन ही के। मिटहिँ दोष दुख भव-रजनी के॥
en: Then the pure eyes of the heart open, and the faults and sorrows of the night of worldly life are gone; the jewels of Rama's story, hidden or seen, in whatever mine they lie, become visible.

first: दो॰—जथा सुअञ्जन अञ्जि दृग, साधक सिद्ध सुजान।
en: Just as seekers who put a magic salve on their eyes become perfected and wise, and then see with ease the treasures in hills, forests and under the earth.

first: चौ॰—गुरु-पद-रज मृदु मञ्जुल अञ्जन। नयन-अमिय दृग दोष बिभञ्जन।
en: The dust of the Guru's feet is a soft and lovely salve, nectar for the eyes that cures their faults; with it I clean the eyes of wisdom and tell Rama's story, which frees from the round of birth.

first: बन्दउँ प्रथम महोसुरचरना। माह जनित संसय सब हरना॥
en: First I bow to the feet of the Brahmins, gods on earth, who remove all doubts born of ignorance; then with love and kind words I bow to the gathering of good people, a mine of all virtues.

first: साधु चरित सुभ सरिस कपासू। निरस बिसद गुन-मय फल जासू॥
en: The life of the good is like cotton, gentle and pure; its fruit is dry but white and full of thread; it bears pain itself to cover the holes of others, and so it has won praise in the world.

first: मुद-मङ्गल-मय सन्त-समाजू। जो जग जङ्गम तीरथराजू॥
en: The gathering of saints, full of joy and blessing, is a moving Prayag, king of holy places, in the world; there devotion to Rama is the Ganga, and the spread of thought on Brahman is the Saraswati.

first: विधि-निषेध-मय कलिमल-हरनी। करम कथा रविनन्दिनि बरनी॥
en: Talk of duties to do and not to do, which removes the sins of the age, is the Yamuna; and talk of Hari and Hara shines as the meeting of the three rivers, giving joy and blessing to all who hear.

first: बट बिस्वास अचल निज-धर्मा। तीरथराज-समाज सुकर्मा॥
en: Firm faith in one's own duty is the undying banyan tree, and good deeds are the crowd of pilgrims; this Prayag is easy for all, on every day and in every land, and serving it with respect ends all pain.

first: अकथ अलौकिक तीरथराऊ। देइ सद्य फल प्रगट प्रमाऊ॥७॥
en: This king of holy places is beyond words and beyond this world; it gives its fruit at once, and its power is plain to see.

first: दो॰ – सुनि समुझहिँ जन मुदित मन, मज्जहिँ अति अनुराग।
en: Those who hear and understand with a glad heart and bathe in it with deep love gain the four goals of life while still in this body; such is the Prayag of the saints.

first: चौ॰ – मज्जन फल पेखिय ततकाला। काक होहिं पिक बकउ मराला॥
en: The fruit of this bathing is seen at once: crows become cuckoos and cranes become swans. Let no one be surprised on hearing this, for the glory of good company is no secret.

first: बालमीकि नारद घटजोनी। निज निज मुखनि कही निज होनी॥
en: Valmiki, Narada and Agastya each told with their own lips how they came to be what they were; and all the many beings in water, on land and in the sky, moving or still, in this world,

first: मति कीरति गति भूति भलाई। जब जेहि जतन जहाँ जेहि पाई।।
en: whatever wisdom, fame, salvation, wealth or good any of them has gained, at any time, by any means, anywhere, know it as the power of good company; neither the world nor the Vedas know another way.

first: बिनु सतसङ्ग बिबेक न होई। राम-कृपा-बिनु सुलम न सोई॥
en: Without good company there is no wisdom, and without Rama's grace good company is not easy to find. Good company is the root of joy and blessing; it is the fruit, and all other practices are only the flowers.

first: सठ सुधरहिँ सतसङ्गति पाई। पारस परस कुधातु सुहाई॥
en: Even the wicked improve in good company, as base metal turns to gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone; and if by fate the good fall into bad company, they keep their own nature, like the jewel in a snake's head.

first: बिधि हरि हर कबि कोबिद बानी। कहत साधु-महिमा सकुचानी॥
en: The words of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, poets and scholars falter when they try to tell the glory of the saints; I cannot tell it any more than a vegetable seller can tell the worth of jewels.

first: दो॰ – बन्दउँ सन्त समान चित, हित अनहित नहिं कोउ।
en: I bow to the saints, whose minds are even, who have no friend and no enemy; like a fine flower held in the hollow of the hands, they give the same sweet scent to both hands.

first: सन्त सरल चित जगत हित, जानि सुभाउ सनेहु।
en: Saints are simple at heart and good to the whole world; knowing this loving nature of theirs, I pray: hear this child's request, see his good wish, and give me love for Rama's feet.

first: चौ॰ – बहुरिवन्दि खलगन सतिभाये। जे बिनु काज दाहिनेहुँ बाँये।
en: Now I bow with a true heart to the crowd of wicked people, who turn against even those who help them, for no reason; to them another's loss is gain, they rejoice when others are ruined and grieve when others prosper.

first: हरि-हर-जस राकेस राहु से। पर अकाज भट सहसबाहु से॥
en: They are like Rahu to the full moon of the fame of Hari and Hara, and great fighters like Sahasrabahu in spoiling others' work; they see others' faults with a thousand eyes, and fall like a fly into the ghee of others' good, spoiling it.

first: तेज-कृपानु रोष महिषेसा। अघ-अवगुन-धन धनी धनेसा॥
en: In heat they are fire, in anger they are Yama; in the wealth of sin and vice they are rich as Kubera; their rise brings harm to all like a comet, and like Kumbhakarna it is best when they sleep.

first: पर अकाज लगि तनु परिहरहीं। जिमि हिम-उपल कृषी दलि गरहीं॥
en: To harm others they will give up even their own bodies, as hail destroys the crop and then melts away. I bow to the wicked as to the angry Shesha, who with a thousand mouths tells the faults of others.

first: पुनि प्रनववोँ पृथुराज समाना। पर अघ सुनइ सहस-दस-काना॥
en: Again I bow to them as to King Prithu, who hears others' sins with ten thousand ears; and I pray to them as to Indra, who always loves wine (and the army of the gods),

first: बचन बज्र जेहि सदा पियारा। सहस-नयन पर दोष निहारा॥६॥
en: who always loves the thunderbolt of harsh words, and looks at others' faults with a thousand eyes.

first: दो॰ – उदासीन-अरि-मीत-हित, सुनत जरहिं खल रीति।
en: The way of the wicked is to burn on hearing of the good of anyone, whether stranger, enemy or friend; knowing this, this servant still joins both hands and prays to them with love.

first: चौ॰ – में अपनी दिसि कीन्ह निहोरा। तिन्ह निज ओर न लाउब भोरा॥
en: I have made my request from my side, but they will never fail to act as they are from theirs; raise a crow with all the love you like, will it ever stop eating flesh?

first: बन्दउँ सन्त असज्जन चरना। दुख-प्रद-उभय बीच कछु धरना।
en: I bow to the feet of both saints and wicked people; both cause pain, but with a difference: the one takes our life away when he parts from us, the other gives terrible pain when he meets us.

first: उपजहिँ एक सङ्ग जग माहीं। जलज जोँक जिमि गुन बिलगाहीं॥
en: Both are born together in the world, yet their natures differ like the lotus and the leech, both born of water; good and bad are like nectar and wine, both born of the one deep ocean of the world.

first: भल अनभलनिजनिज करतूती। लहत सुजस अपलोक बिभूती॥
en: Good and bad, each by their own deeds, gain good fame or ill fame; the good are like nectar, the moon and the Ganga, while the wicked are like poison, fire and the river of sin.

first: गुन अवगुन जानत सब कोई। जो जेहि भाव नीक तेहि सोई॥५॥
en: Everyone knows what is good and what is bad, but each likes what suits his own nature.

first: दो॰ – भलो भलाइहि पै लहइ, लहइ निचाइहि नीचु।
en: The good gain only goodness and the low gain only lowness; nectar is praised for giving life without death, and poison is praised for giving death.

first: चौ॰ – खल-अघ-अगुन साधु-गुन-गाहा। उभय अपार उदधि अवगाहा॥
en: The tale of the sins and faults of the wicked and of the virtues of the saints are both endless, deep oceans; I have described some good and bad only because one cannot take or leave a thing without knowing it.

first: भलेउ पोच सब विधि उपजाये। गनि गुन दोष बेद बिलगाये॥
en: Good and bad were both made by the Creator, and the Vedas have set apart their merits and faults; the Vedas, histories and Puranas say the Creator's world is a mix of good and bad.

first: दुख-सुख पाप-पुन्य दिन-राती। साधु-असाधु सुजाति-कुजाती॥
en: Pain and joy, sin and merit, day and night, saint and sinner, high birth and low birth, demon and god, high and low, life-giving nectar and deadly poison,

first: माया ब्रह्म जीव-जगदीसा। लच्छि-अलच्छि रङ्क-अवनीसा॥
en: maya and Brahman, the soul and the Lord, wealth and want, beggar and king, Kashi and Magadh, the Ganga and the Karmanasha, desert Marwar and fertile Malwa, Brahmin and butcher,

first: सरग-नरक अनुराग-बिरागा। निगम-अगम गुन-दोष-विभागा॥५॥
en: heaven and hell, love and detachment: the Vedas and scriptures have sorted out the good and bad in all these.

first: दो॰ – जड़-चेतन गुन-दोष मय, बिस्व कीन्ह करतार।
en: The Creator made the world of moving and still things, a mix of good and bad; the swan-like saints drink the milk of good and leave behind the water of bad.

first: चौ॰ – अस बिबेक जब देइ बिधाता। तब तजि दोष गुनहि मन राता॥
en: When the Creator gives this kind of judgment, the mind leaves faults and delights in virtues; yet by the force of time, nature and karma, even good people under maya's sway may fail in goodness.

first: सो सुधारि हरिजन जिमि लेहीँ। दलि दुख दोष बिमल जस देहीं।
en: Devotees of Hari put that slip right, crush the pain and fault, and give pure fame; the wicked too may do good in good company, but their low nature never changes.

first: लखि सुबेष जग बञ्चक जेऊ। बेष प्रताप पूजियहि तेऊ।
en: Even cheats are worshipped by the world when it sees their fine dress, by the power of that dress; but in the end they are found out and cannot keep it up, like Kalanemi, Ravana and Rahu.

first: किये कुबेष साधु सनमानू। जिमि जग जामवन्त हनुमानू॥
en: The good are honoured even in poor dress, like Jambavan and Hanuman in the world. That bad company brings loss and good company brings gain is known to all, in the world and in the Vedas.

first: गगन चढ़इ रज पवन प्रसङ्गा। कोचहि मिलइ नीच जल सङ्गा॥
en: Dust rises to the sky with the wind, and falls into the mud with low-flowing water; parrots and mynas in good homes repeat Rama's name, while in bad homes they repeat curse after curse.

first: धूम कुसङ्गति कारिख होई। लिखिय पुरान मज्जु मसि सोई॥
en: In bad company smoke becomes soot, yet the same soot becomes fine ink for writing the Puranas; and joined with water, fire and wind it becomes the cloud that gives life to the world.

first: दो॰ – ग्रह भेषज जल पवन पट, पाइ कुजोग सुजोग।
en: Planets, medicines, water, wind and cloth become bad or good in the world by bad or good company; people of good sense see this.

first: सम प्रकास तम पाख दुहुँ, नाम भेद बिधि कीन्ह।
en: Both halves of the month have equal light and dark, but the Creator gave them different names; the world praises the one as feeding the moon and blames the other as wasting it.

first: जड़ चेतन जग जीव जत, सकल राम-मय जानि।
en: Knowing all beings in the world, moving and still, to be full of Rama, I always bow at the lotus feet of all with joined hands.

first: देव दनुज नर नाग खग, प्रेत पितर गन्धर्व।
en: Gods, demons, men, serpents, birds, ghosts, ancestors, Gandharvas, Kinnaras and night-wanderers, I bow to you all; now all of you, be kind to me.

first: चौ॰ – आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल-थल-नभ-वासी॥
en: Knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Rama, all beings of the four kinds of birth and eighty-four lakh species, living in water, on land and in the sky, I bow with joined hands.

first: जानि कृपाकर किङ्कर मोहू। सब मिलि करहु छाड़ि छल छोहू॥
en: Knowing me as your servant, all of you together, be kind to me and leave aside deceit. I have no trust in the strength of my own mind, so I make this request to all.

first: करन चहउँ रघुपति-गुन-गाहा। लघु-मति-मोरि चरित अवगाहा।
en: I want to tell the virtues of Raghupati, but my mind is small and his story is very deep; I cannot see even one part of a way to do it; my mind and wit are poor, but my wish is like a king.

first: मति अति नीच ऊँचि रुचि आछी। चहिय अमिय जग जुरइ न छाछी॥
en: My mind is very low but my desire is high and fine; I want nectar, yet I cannot even find buttermilk in the world. The good will forgive my boldness and listen with care to a child's words.

first: जौं बालक कह तोतरि बाता। सुनहिँ मुदित मन पितु अरु माता॥
en: When a child speaks in a lisping voice, his father and mother listen with glad hearts; but cruel, crooked and evil-minded people, who wear others' faults as ornaments, will laugh.

first: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥
en: Who does not like his own poetry, whether it is rich in taste or quite dull? But those who are glad to hear the poetry of others, such fine people are not many in the world.

first: जग बहु नर सरि सर सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई।
en: Brother, many people in the world are like rivers and ponds, which swell only with their own water; rare is the good person like the ocean, who swells on seeing the full moon, the good of another.

first: दो॰ – भाग छोट अभिलाष बड़, करउँ एक बिस्वास।
en: My fortune is small and my desire is large, but I trust one thing: the good will be happy to hear this, and the wicked will laugh at it.

first: चौ॰ – खल परिहास होइ हित मोरा। काक कहहिं कलकंठ कठोरा॥
en: The mocking of the wicked will do me good: crows call the sweet-voiced cuckoo harsh, cranes laugh at swans and frogs at the chataka bird; so do the foul wicked laugh at pure speech.

first: कबित रसिक न राम-पद-नेहू। तिन्ह कहँ सुखद हासरस एहू॥
en: For those who neither love poetry nor love Rama's feet, this work will be a source of laughter and fun; it is in the common tongue and my mind is simple, so it is fit to be laughed at, and they are not to blame.

first: प्रभु-पद-प्रीति न साभुक्ति नीकी। तिन्हहिं कथा सुनि लागिहि फीकी॥
en: Those who have no love for the Lord's feet and no good sense will find this story dull; but those who love the feet of Hari and Hara and do not argue for argument's sake will find Raghubar's story sweet.

first: रामगति-भूषित जिय जानी। सुनिहहिं सुजन सराहि सुबानी॥
en: Knowing in their hearts that it is adorned with devotion to Rama, the good will listen and praise it with kind words. I am no poet, nor clever or skilled; I lack every art and all learning.

first: आखर अरथ अलंकृत नाना। छन्द प्रबन्ध अनेक विधाना॥
en: There are letters, meanings, many kinds of ornament, many metres and forms of composition, endless kinds of feeling and taste, and many kinds of faults and merits in poetry;

first: कबित बिबेक एक नहिं मोरे। सत्य कहउँ लिखि कागद कोरे॥६॥
en: I do not have even one skill in judging poetry; I say this truly, writing it on blank paper.

first: दो॰ – भनिति मोरि सब गुन रहित, विस्व विदित गुन एक।
en: My speech lacks every merit, but it has one merit known to the whole world; thinking of that, wise people with pure judgment will listen to it.

first: चौ॰ – एहि महँ रघुपति नाम उदारा। अति पावन पुरान-स्रुति-सारा॥
en: In it is the noble name of Raghupati, most holy, the essence of the Puranas and Vedas, home of blessing and remover of misfortune, which Shiva repeats along with Uma.

first: भनिति बिचित्र सुकबि कृत जोऊ। राम नाम बिनु सोह न सोऊ॥
en: Even fine and wonderful poetry by a good poet does not shine without Rama's name, just as a lovely moon-faced woman, fully adorned, does not look fine without clothes.

first: सब गुन रहित कुकबि कृत बानी। राम नाम जस अङ्कित जानी॥
en: Even verse without any merit, by a poor poet, if marked with the fame of Rama's name, the wise recite and hear with respect, for saints, like bees, take only the good.

first: जदपि कबित रस एकउ नाहीं। राम-प्रताप प्रगट एहि माहीं।
en: Though this has not one taste of true poetry, Rama's glory is plain in it; that is the hope that comes to my mind: who has not gained greatness from good company?

first: धूमउ तजइ सहज करुआई। अगर प्रसङ्ग सुगन्ध बसाई
en: Even smoke gives up its natural bitterness and takes on a sweet scent in the company of aloe wood; my speech is rough, but it tells a good thing, Rama's story, which brings blessing to the world.

first: मङ्गल-करनि कलिमल-हरनि तुलसी कथा रघुनाथ की।
en: Tulsi says the story of Raghunath brings blessing and removes the sins of the age; the course of this river of poetry is winding like that of holy rivers; joined with the Lord's fame, my poor verse will please the good, as cremation ash on Shiva's body is lovely and purifying to remember.

first: दो॰ – प्रिय लागिहि अति सबहि मम, भनिति ति राम-जस-सङ्ग।
en: Because it goes with Rama's fame, my verse will be very dear to all; when sandal from the Malaya hills is honoured, does anyone think of it as mere wood?

first: स्याम-सुरभि-पय बिसद अति, गुनद-करहिं सब पान।
en: Everyone drinks the milk of a black cow, knowing it to be very white and healthy; so the wise sing and hear the fame of Sita and Rama even in a village tongue.

first: चौ॰ – मनि-मानिक-मुकता-छबि जैसी।अहि-गिरि-गज-सिरसोहनतैसी।
en: Gems, rubies and pearls do not shine as they should on the head of a snake, a mountain or an elephant; set in a king's crown or on a young woman's body, they gain far greater beauty.

first: तैसेहि सुकबि कबित बुध कहहीं। उपजहिँ अनत अनत छबि लहहीं॥
en: In the same way, the wise say, a good poet's verse is born in one place and shines in another. When a poet remembers Saraswati, she leaves Brahma's home and comes running, out of devotion.

first: रामचरितसर बिनु अन्हवाये। सो सम जाइ न कोटि उपाये॥
en: Unless she is bathed in the lake of Rama's story, her weariness does not go by millions of means; knowing this in their hearts, poets and scholars sing the fame of Hari, which removes the sins of the age.

first: कीन्हे प्राकृत-जन गुनगाना। सिर धुनि गिरा लगति पछिताना।
en: When poets sing the praises of ordinary men, Saraswati beats her head in regret. The wise say the poet's heart is the ocean, his mind is the oyster shell, and Saraswati is the Swati star.

first: जौं बरषद बर-बारि बिचारू। होहिँ कबित-मुकता-मनि चारू॥५॥
en: If a rain of fine thought falls, lovely pearls and gems of poetry are formed.

first: दो॰ – जुगुति बेधि पुनि पोहियहि, रामचरित बर ताग।
en: Pierce them with the needle of skill and string them on the fine thread of Rama's story; the good wear it on their pure hearts, and its beauty is great love.

first: चौ॰ – जे जनमे कलिकाल कराला। करतब बायस बेष मराला॥
en: Those born in this terrible Kali age, who act like crows but dress like swans, who leave the path of the Vedas and walk a bad road, bodies of deceit and pots full of the age's filth,

first: बञ्चक भगत कहाइ राम के। किङ्कर कञ्चन कोह-काम के।
en: cheats who call themselves Rama's devotees but are slaves of gold, anger and lust; among them I am counted first in the world, a hypocrite who flies the flag of religion and carries the burden of worldly business.

first: जौं अपने अवगुन सब कहऊँ। बाढ़इ कथा पार नहिँ लहऊँ॥
en: If I told all my faults, the story would grow so long I would never reach the end; so I have said very little, and the wise will understand from a little.

first: समुझि बिबिध बिधि बिनती मोरी। कोउ न कथा सुनि देइहि खोरी॥
en: Seeing my many kinds of request, no one hearing the story will blame me; anyone who still finds fault is even more foolish and poor in mind than I am.

first: कबि न होउँ नहिं चतुर कहावउँ। मति अनुरूप राम-गुन गावउँ॥
en: I am no poet and I do not want to be called clever; I sing Rama's virtues as far as my mind allows. Where is Raghupati's endless story, and where is my mind, caught up in the world?

first: जेहि मारुत गिरि मेरु उड़ाहीँ। कहहु तूल केहि लेखे माहीं॥
en: Tell me, where a wind blows that sweeps away great mountains like Meru, what count is cotton? Knowing Rama's boundless greatness, my mind is very fearful as I tell the story.

first: दो॰ – सारद सेष महेस बिधि, आगम निगम पुरान।
en: Saraswati, Shesha, Shiva, Brahma, the scriptures, Vedas and Puranas sing his virtues all the time, yet say 'not this, not this'.

first: चौ॰ – सब जानत प्रभु प्रभुता सोई। तदपि कहे बिनु रहा न कोई॥
en: All know that the Lord's greatness is like that, yet no one could stay without speaking of it; for this the Vedas gave the reason, saying in many ways what power there is in worship.

first: एक अनीह अरूप अनामा। अज सच्चिदानन्द परधामा॥
en: The one Lord, without desire, form or name, unborn, being, awareness and bliss, the highest home, present everywhere, the universe itself, took a body and did many deeds.

first: सो केवल भगतन्ह हित लागी। परम कृपाल प्रनत-अनुरागी॥
en: He did this only for the good of his devotees, being most kind and loving to those who bow to him; he holds his servants dear and has great tender care for them, and once he shows mercy he never turns angry.

first: गई बहोर गरीब-नेवाजू। सरल सबल साहिब रघुराजू॥
en: Raghuraj, the king of Raghu's line, restores what was lost, cares for the poor, and is a simple yet mighty master; knowing this, the wise tell Hari's fame and make their speech holy and fruitful.

first: तेहि बल मैं रघुपति गुन-गाथा। कहिहउँ नाइ राम-पद माथा।
en: With that strength I will bow my head at Rama's feet and tell the tale of Raghupati's virtues; the sages sang Hari's fame before me, and walking their path is easy for me, brother.

first: दो॰ – अति अपार जे सरित बर, जौँ नृप सेतु कराहिँ।
en: If a king builds a bridge over a very wide river, even the tiniest ant can climb on it and cross without effort.

first: चौ॰ – एहि प्रकार बल मनहिँ देखाई। करिहउँ रघुपति कथा सुहाई।।
en: Giving my mind such strength, I will tell the lovely story of Raghupati. Vyasa and the first poet Valmiki and many great poets have told Hari's fame with reverence.

first: चरन-कमल बन्दउँ तिन्ह केरे। पुरवहुँ सकल मनोरथ मेरे॥
en: I bow at their lotus feet; may they fulfil all my wishes. I bow to the poets of the Kali age who have described the many virtues of Raghupati.

first: जे प्राकृति कबि परम सयाने। भाषा जिन्ह हरि चरित बखाने॥
en: I bow without deceit to all the very wise poets of the common tongue who have told Hari's story in the people's language, those who were, who are, and who will be.

first: होहु प्रसन्न देहु बरदानू। साधु-समाज भनिति सनमानू॥
en: Be pleased and give me this blessing, that my verse be honoured among good people; a work the wise do not honour is labour wasted by foolish poets.

first: कीरति भनिति भूति भलि सोई। सुरसरि सम सब कहँ हित होई॥
en: Fame, poetry and wealth are good only when, like the Ganga, they do good to all. Rama's fame is lovely but my speech is rough; this mismatch is my worry.

first: तुम्हरी कृपा सुलभ सोउ मोरे। सियनि सुहावनि टाट पटोरे॥६॥
en: By your grace even that becomes easy for me; good stitching looks fine whether on sackcloth or silk.

first: दो॰ – सरल कबित कीरति बिमल, सोइ आदरहिं सुजान।
en: The wise honour poetry that is simple and tells of pure fame, which even an enemy, forgetting his natural hatred, praises on hearing it.

first: सो न होइ बिनु बिमल मति, मोहि मति-बल अति थोर।
en: Such poetry cannot come without a pure mind, and my mind is very weak; so again and again I pray, be kind so that I may tell Hari's fame.

first: कबि कोबिद रघुबर-चरित, मानस मञ्जु मराल।
en: Poets and scholars, you are lovely swans on the Manas lake of Raghubar's story; hearing this child's prayer and seeing his good wish, be kind to me.

first: सो॰ – बन्दउँ मुनि-पद-कञ्जु, रामायन जेहिं निरमयेउ।
en: I bow at the lotus feet of the sage Valmiki who made the Ramayana, which tells of Khara yet is soft and lovely, and tells of Dushana yet is free of faults.

first: बन्दउँ चारिउ बेद, भव-बारिधि-बोहित सरिस।
en: I bow to the four Vedas, which are like ships to cross the ocean of worldly life, and which never tire, even in a dream, of telling Raghubar's pure fame.

first: बन्दउँ बिधि-पद-रेनु, भव-सागर जेहि कीन्ह जहँ।
en: I bow to the dust of Brahma's feet, who made the ocean of worldly life, from which came the saints as nectar, moon and wish-giving cow, and the wicked as poison and wine.

first: दो॰ – बिबुध बिप्र बुध ग्रह चरन, बन्दि कहउँ कर जोरि।
en: Bowing at the feet of gods, Brahmins, scholars and the planets, I say with joined hands: be pleased and fulfil all my fine wishes.

first: चौ॰ – पुनि बन्दउँ सारद सुरसरिता। जुगल पुनीत मनोहर-चरिता॥
en: Then I bow to Saraswati and to the Ganga, both holy and lovely in their ways; one removes sin when one bathes in it and drinks it, the other removes ignorance when it is spoken and heard.

first: गुरु पितु मातु महेस-भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबन्धु दिन-दानी॥
en: I bow to Mahesh and Bhavani, my Guru, father and mother, friends of the humble and daily givers, who are servant, master and friend of Sita's lord, and in every way the true well-wishers of Tulsi.

first: कलि बिलोकि जग-हित हर-गिरजा। साबर मन्त्र जाल जिन्ह सिरजा।
en: Seeing the Kali age, Shiva and Parvati, for the good of the world, made the Shabar spells; their letters do not fit, they have no meaning and no proper way of chanting, yet their power is plain through Shiva's might.

first: सो महेस मोहि पर अनुकूला। करउँ कथा मुद-मङ्गल-मूला॥
en: That Shiva is kind to me, so I tell this story, the root of joy and blessing; remembering Shiva and Parvati and gaining their favour, I tell Rama's story with an eager heart.

first: भनिति मोरि सिव कृपा बिभाती। ससि-समाज मिलि मनहुँ सुराती।
en: By Shiva's grace my verse shines like a fine night with the moon and stars. Those who tell or hear this story with love, understanding it with care,

first: होइहहिँ राम-चरन-अनुरागी। कलिमल-रहित सुमङ्गल-भागी॥६॥
en: will come to love Rama's feet, be freed from the sins of the age, and share in true blessing.

first: दो॰ – सपनेहुँ साँचेहु मोहि पर, जौँ हर-गौरि-पसाउ।
en: If the favour of Hara and Gauri is truly on me, even in a dream, then all I have said of the power of this verse in the common tongue will come true.

first: चौ॰ – बन्दउँ अवधपुरी अतिपावनि। सरजू-सरि कलि-कलुष-नसावनि॥
en: I bow to the most holy city of Ayodhya and to the Sarayu river, which destroys the sins of the age; then I bow to the men and women of that city, whom the Lord loves dearly.

first: सिय-निन्दक अघ-ओघ नसाये। लोक बिसाक बनाइ बसाये।
en: He destroyed the heap of sins of the one who blamed Sita, freed him from grief and gave him a home in his own world. I bow to Kausalya, who is like the eastern sky, whose fame fills the whole world,

first: प्रगटेउ जहँ रघुपति ससि चारू। बिस्व-सुखद खल-कमल-तुसारू॥
en: for from her rose Raghupati like a lovely moon, giving joy to the world and being frost to the lotus-like wicked. I think of King Dasharath with all his queens as merit and blessing in bodily form,

first: करउँ प्रनाम करम-मन-बानी। करहु कृपा सुत-सेवक जानी॥
en: and I bow to them in deed, thought and word: be kind to me, knowing me as your son's servant. By making them the Creator became great, for Rama's father and mother are the very limit of glory.

first: सो॰ – बन्दउँ अवध भुआल, सत्य प्रेम जेहि राम पद।
en: I bow to the king of Ayodhya, who had true love for Rama's feet, and who gave up his dear body like a blade of grass when parted from the Lord, kind to the humble.

first: चौ॰ – प्रनवउँ परिजन सहित बिदेहू। जाहि राम-पद गूढ़-सनेहू॥
en: I bow to Videha (King Janak) with his family, who had a deep, hidden love for Rama's feet; he kept it hidden under yoga and royal life, but it showed itself when he saw Rama.

first: प्रनवउँ प्रथम भरत के चरना। जासु नेम ब्रत जाइ न बरना॥
en: First of the brothers, I bow at the feet of Bharat, whose vows and discipline cannot be described, whose mind, like a greedy bee, never leaves the lotus feet of Rama.

first: बन्दउँ लछिमन-पद-जल जाता । सीतल सुभग भगत-सुखदाता॥
en: I bow at Lakshman's lotus feet, cool, lovely and a joy to devotees; Raghupati's fame is a pure flag, and Lakshman's fame is the staff that holds it up.

first: सेष सहस्त्र-सीस जग कारन। जो अवतरेउ भूमि-भय-टारन॥
en: He is the thousand-headed Shesha, support of the world, who came down to remove the earth's fear; may Sumitra's son, ocean of mercy and mine of virtues, always be kind to me.

first: रिपुसूदन पद कमल नमामी। सूर सुसील भरत अनुगामी॥
en: I bow at the lotus feet of Shatrughna, brave and gentle, who follows Bharat. I pray to the great hero Hanuman, whose fame Rama himself has told.

first: सो॰ – प्रनवउँ पवन कुमार, खल बन पावक ज्ञान घन।
en: I bow to the son of the Wind, a fire to the forest of the wicked, a mass of wisdom, in whose heart lives Rama, holding bow and arrows.

first: ची॰ – कपिपति रीछ निसाचर राजा। अङ्गदादि जे कीस-समाजा॥
en: Sugriva lord of the monkeys, Jambavan king of the bears, Vibhishana king of the demons, and all the monkey host led by Angad: I bow to their lovely feet, who found Rama though born in low bodies.

first: रघुपति चरन उपासक जेते। खग मृग सुर नर असुर समेते॥
en: All who worship Raghupati's feet, birds, beasts, gods, men and demons, who serve Rama without any selfish wish, I bow at all their lotus feet.

first: सुक सनकादि भगत मुनि नारद। जे मुनिवर बिज्ञान बिसारद॥
en: Shuka, Sanaka and his brothers, the devotee Narada, and all the great sages skilled in true knowledge: I bow to them all with my head to the ground; great sages, be kind, knowing me as your servant.

first: जनक-सुता जग-जननि जानकी। अतिसय प्रिय करना निधान की।
en: Janaki, daughter of Janak, mother of the world, most dear to Rama the store of mercy: I pray to her two lotus feet, by whose grace I may gain a pure mind.

first: पुनि मन-बचन-करम रघुनायक। चरन-कमल बन्दउँ सब लायक॥
en: Then in mind, word and deed I bow at the lotus feet of Raghunayak, able in every way, lotus-eyed, holding bow and arrow, who removes his devotees' troubles and gives them joy.

first: दो॰ – गिरा-अरथ जल-बीचि सम, कहियत भिन्न न भिन्न।
en: Word and meaning, like water and wave, are called different but are not different; I bow at the feet of Sita and Rama, who hold the humble most dear.

first: चौ॰ – बन्दउँ नाम राम रघुबर को। हेतु कृसानु-भानु-हिमकर को।
en: I bow to the name 'Rama' of Raghubar, the source of fire, sun and moon; it is Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva in one, the life of the Vedas, beyond qualities, beyond compare, and a store of virtues.

first: महा मन्त्र जोइ जपत महेसू। कासी मुकुति हेतु उपदेसू॥
en: It is the great mantra Shiva repeats, and the teaching that gives freedom in Kashi; Ganesha knows its glory, for he is worshipped first by the power of the name.

first: जान आदिकबि नाम-प्रतापू। भयउ सुद्ध करि उलटा जापू॥
en: The first poet knew the name's power, for he became pure by repeating it backwards; hearing from Shiva that it equals the thousand names, Bhavani repeats it and then eats with her beloved.

first: हरषे हेतु हेरि हर ही को। किय भूषन तिय भूषन ती को।
en: Seeing such love in her heart, Shiva was glad and made her, the jewel among women, his own ornament (half his body). Shiva knows the power of the name well, for it turned deadly poison into nectar for him.

first: दो॰ – बरषा रितु रघुपति भगति, तुलसी सालि सुदास।
en: Tulsi says: devotion to Raghupati is the rainy season, good devotees are the rice plants, and the two fine letters of Rama's name are the months of Sawan and Bhadon.

first: चौ॰ – आखर मधुर मनोहर दोऊ। बरन बिलोचन जन जिय जोऊ॥
en: The two letters are sweet and lovely, the eyes of the alphabet and the life of devotees; easy to remember and a joy to all, they give gain in this world and support in the next.

first: कहत सुनत सुमिरत सुठि नीके। राम-लखन-सम प्रिय तुलसी के॥
en: They are very fine to say, to hear and to remember, and dear to Tulsi as Rama and Lakshman; when spoken they seem separate, but they are natural companions, like Brahman and the soul.

first: नर-नारायन-सरिस सुभ्राता। जग पालक बिसेष जन त्राता॥
en: They are fine brothers like Nara and Narayana, keepers of the world and special saviours of devotees; they are lovely earrings for the fair lady Devotion, and the pure moon and sun for the good of the world.

first: स्वाद तोष सम सुगति सुधा के। कमठ सेष सम धर बसुधा के॥
en: They are like the taste and the fullness of the nectar of salvation, like the Tortoise and Shesha who hold up the earth, like bees to the lovely lotus of the devotee's mind, and like Krishna and Balaram to the Yashoda of the tongue.

first: दो॰ – एक छत्र एक मुकुट-मनि, सब बरनन्हि पर जोउ।
en: Tulsi says the two letters of Raghubar's name shine above all letters, one as the royal umbrella and the other as the jewel in the crown.

first: चौ॰ – समुझत सरिस नाम अरु नामी। प्रीति परसपर प्रभु अनुगामी॥
en: Rightly understood, the name and the one it names are alike, and their love for each other is like that of master and follower; name and form are two marks of the Lord, beyond words, without beginning, known only by true understanding.

first: को बड़ छोट कहत अपराधू। सुनि गुन भेद समुझिहहिँ साधू॥
en: To say which is greater or smaller is a fault; hearing their qualities, good people will understand the difference. We see that form depends on name, and without the name the form cannot be known.

first: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जाने। करतल गत न परहिँ पहिचाने।
en: Even a special form, though held in the palm, cannot be recognised without knowing its name; but if one remembers the name without seeing the form, a special love comes into the heart.

first: नाम-रूप-गुन अकथ कहानी। समुझत सुखद न परति बखानी॥
en: The story of the virtues of name and form cannot be told; it gives joy to understand but cannot be put in words. Between the Lord without form and the Lord with form, the name is a good witness, a clever interpreter that makes both known.

first: दो॰ – राम-नाममनि-दीप धरु, जीह देहरी-द्वार।
en: Tulsi says: if you want light inside and outside, place the jewel-lamp of Rama's name on the threshold of your tongue.

first: चौ॰ – नाम जीह जपि जागहीँ जोगी। विरति बिरञ्चि प्रपञ्च वियोगी।
en: Yogis stay awake by repeating the name on their tongues, free of desire and cut off from the Creator's world; they taste the matchless bliss of Brahman, beyond words, beyond pain, without name or form.

first: जाना चहहिं गूढ़ गति जेऊ। नाम जीह जपि जानहिँ तेऊ॥
en: Those who want to know the hidden truth come to know it by repeating the name; seekers who repeat the name with full attention become perfected and gain powers like becoming tiny.

first: जपहिँ नाम जन आरत भारी। मिटहिँ कुसङ्कट होहिं सुखारी॥
en: Devotees in great distress repeat the name, and their hard troubles end and they become happy. There are four kinds of Rama's devotees in the world, and all four are good, sinless and noble.

first: चहूँ चतुर कहँ नाम अधारा। ज्ञानी प्रभुहि बिसेष पियारा॥
en: All four wise kinds rely on the name, but the one who knows is especially dear to the Lord. In all four ages and in all four Vedas the name has power, and in the Kali age above all, for there is no other way.

first: दो॰ – सकल कामना हीन जे, राम भगति रस लीन।
en: Even those who are free of all desire and lost in the joy of devotion to Rama have made their minds into fish in the lake of nectar of love for the name.

first: चौ॰ – अगुनसगुनदुइ ब्रह्म सरूपा। अकथ अगाध अनादि अनूपा॥
en: Brahman has two forms, with qualities and without; both are beyond words, deep, without beginning and beyond compare. In my view the name is greater than both, for by its own power it has brought both under its control.

first: प्रौढ़ सुजन जनि जानहिं जन की। कहउँ प्रतीति प्रीति रुचि मन की॥
en: Let the wise not take this as a mere servant's boldness; I speak of the faith, love and liking of my heart. Knowledge of Brahman in two forms is like fire: one is hidden inside wood, the other is seen burning.

first: उभय अगम जुग सुगम नाम तेँ। कहउँ नाम बड़ ब्रह्म राम तें॥
en: Both are hard to reach, but both become easy through the name; so I say the name is greater than both Brahman and Rama. Brahman is one, everywhere, undying, being and awareness, a mass of bliss.

first: अस प्रभु हृदय अछत अबिकारी। सकल जीव जग दीन दुखारी॥
en: Though such a Lord lives in the heart, unchanging, all beings in the world are poor and suffering; but by making the name known and working at it, he too is revealed, as a jewel's worth is seen when it is tested.

first: दो॰ – निरगुन ते एहि भाँति बड़, नाम प्रभाउ अपार।
en: In this way the name, with its endless power, is greater than Brahman without form; now, by my own thinking, I say how the name is greater than Rama.

first: चौ॰ – राम भगत हित नर तनु धारी। सहि सङ्कट किय साधु सुखारी॥
en: For his devotees Rama took a human body, bore hardships and made the good happy; by repeating the name with love, devotees become, without effort, a home of joy and blessing.

first: राम एक तापस तिय तारी। नाम कोटि खल कुमति सुधारी॥
en: Rama saved one ascetic's wife (Ahalya), while the name has put right the evil minds of millions of wicked people; for a sage, Rama destroyed Suketu's daughter (Tadaka) with her son and army,

first: सहित दोष-दुख दास दुरासा। दलइ नाम जिमि रबि निसि नासा॥
en: while the name destroys the bad hopes of his servants along with their faults and pains, as the sun ends the night. Rama himself broke Shiva's bow, while the power of the name breaks the fear of worldly life.

first: दंडक बन प्रभु कीन्ह सुहावन। जन-मन-अमित नाम किय पावन॥
en: The Lord made the Dandaka forest lovely, while the name has made pure the minds of countless devotees; Raghunandan crushed hosts of demons, while the name roots out all the sins of the age.

first: दो॰ – सबरी गीध सुसेवकनि, सुगति दीन्हि रघुनाथ।
en: Raghunath gave salvation to good servants like Shabari and the vulture, but the name has saved countless wicked people; its virtues are told in the Vedas.

first: चौ॰ – राम सुकंठ बिभीषन दोऊ। राखे सरन जान सब कोऊ॥
en: Everyone knows that Rama gave shelter to Sugriva and Vibhishana, but the name has blessed many poor people, and its fine fame shines in the world and the Vedas.

first: राम भालु-कपि-कटक बटोरा। सेतु-हेतु स्रम कीन्ह न थोरा॥
en: Rama gathered an army of bears and monkeys and worked hard to build the bridge, but by taking the name the ocean of worldly life dries up; good people, think about this in your hearts.

first: राम सकुल-रन-रावन मारा। सीय सहित निज-पुर पग धारा॥
en: Rama killed Ravana with his family in battle and came back to his city with Sita; Rama became king with Ayodhya as his capital, and gods and sages sing his virtues with fine words,

first: सेवक सुमिरत नाम सप्रीती। बिनु सम प्रबल मोह दल जीती॥
en: while his servants, remembering the name with love, win without effort over the strong army of delusion, and go about lost in love and their own joy; by the grace of the name they have no worry even in a dream.

first: दो॰ – ब्रह्म-राम-तेँ नाम बड़, बरदायक बरदानि।
en: The name is greater than both Brahman and Rama; it gives blessings even to those who give blessings. Knowing this in his heart, Shiva chose it out of the hundred crore verses of Rama's story.

first: चौ॰ – नाम प्रसाद सम्भु अबिनासी। साज-अमङ्गल मङ्गल-रासी।
en: By the grace of the name, Shambhu is undying, and though he wears things of ill omen he is a heap of blessing; Shuka, Sanaka and the perfected ones, sages and yogis enjoy the bliss of Brahman by the grace of the name.

first: नारद जानेउ नाम प्रतापू। जग-प्रिय-हरि हरि-हर-प्रिय आपू॥
en: Narada knew the power of the name, and so, though Hari is dear to the world, Narada is dear to Hari and Hara. By repeating the name Prahlad won the Lord's grace and became the crown of devotees.

first: ध्रुव सगलानि जपेउ हरि-नाऊँ। पायउ अचल अनूपम ठाऊँ।
en: Dhruva, hurt by an insult, repeated Hari's name and gained a fixed and matchless place. By remembering the holy name, the son of the Wind keeps Rama under his control.

first: अपत अजामिल गज गनिकाऊ। भये मुकुत हरि नाम प्रभाऊ॥
en: Even sinful Ajamil, the elephant and the courtesan were freed by the power of Hari's name. How far can I tell the greatness of the name? Even Rama cannot sing all its virtues.

first: दो॰ – नाम राम को कल्पतरु, कलि कल्यान-निवास।
en: In the Kali age Rama's name is the wish-giving tree and the home of all good; by remembering it, Tulsidas, once like worthless hemp, became like the holy tulsi plant.

first: चौ॰ – चहुँ जुग तीनि काल तिहुँ लोका। भये नाम जपि जीव विसोका॥
en: In all four ages, all three times and all three worlds, beings have become free of sorrow by repeating the name. The Vedas, Puranas and saints agree that love for Rama is the fruit of all good deeds.

first: ध्यान प्रथम जुग मख विधि दूजे। द्वापर परितोषन प्रभु पूजे॥
en: In the first age the Lord was pleased by meditation, in the second by sacrifice, and in the third by worship; but the Kali age is only the dirty root of filth, where men's minds are fish in an ocean of sin.

first: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥
en: In this terrible time the name is the wish-giving tree; remembering it ends all the snares of the world. In the Kali age Rama's name gives whatever one wants; it does good in the next world and is father and mother in this one.

first: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलम्बन एकू॥
en: In the Kali age there is no support in rites, devotion or knowledge; Rama's name is the only support. The Kali age is Kalanemi, the store of deceit, and the name is the wise and mighty Hanuman.

first: दो॰ – राम नाम नरकेसरी, कनककसिपु कलिकाल।
en: Rama's name is the Man-Lion, and the Kali age is Hiranyakashipu; it will crush that tormentor of the gods and protect those who repeat the name, as it protected Prahlad.

first: चौ॰ – भाय कुभाय अनख आलसहूँ। नाम जपत मङ्गल दिसि दसहूँ॥
en: Whether with love or ill will, in anger or in laziness, repeating the name brings blessing in all ten directions. Remembering that name and bowing my head to Raghunath, I tell the tale of Rama's virtues.

first: मोरि सुधारिहि सोसब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिँ कृपा अघाती॥
en: He will put right everything for me; his grace never tires of being kind. Rama is a good master and I a bad servant, yet the ocean of mercy has looked to his own nature and cared for me.

first: लोकहु बेद सुसाहिब रीती। बिनय सुनत पहिचानत प्रीती॥
en: In the world and in the Vedas, the way of a good master is to hear a request and see the love behind it. Rich and poor, village folk and city folk, learned and foolish, low and famous,

first: सुकबि कुकबि निज-मति-अनुहारी। नृपहि सराहत सब नर नारी॥
en: good poets and bad, every man and woman praises the king by their own understanding; and the king, good, wise, gentle, born of a part of God and very kind,

first: सुनि सनमानहि सबहि सुबानी। भनिति भगति नति गति पहिचानी॥
en: hears them all and honours each with kind words, seeing their speech, devotion, humility and standing. This is the way of an earthly king; but the lord of Kosala is the crown of the wise,

first: रीझत राम सनेह निसाते। को जग मन्द मलिन-मन मो ते॥६॥
en: and Rama is pleased by pure love alone; yet who in the world is duller and more impure in mind than I am?

first: दो॰ – सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि, रखिहहिँ राम कृपालु।
en: Kind Rama will keep the love and wish of this foolish servant, he who made stones into boats, and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.

first: हौँहुँ कहावत सब कहत, राम सहत उपहास।
en: I too am called his servant and everyone says so, and Rama bears the mockery of having such a servant: a master like the lord of Sita, and a servant like Tulsidas!

first: चौ॰ – अति बड़ि मोरि ढिठाई खोरी। सुनि अघ नरकहुनाक सिकोरी॥
en: Great indeed is my boldness and fault; hearing of my sin, even hell turns up its nose. Knowing this, I shrink with my own imagined fear; but Rama has not given it a thought, even in a dream.

first: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥
en: Hearing, seeing and looking with the eyes of a calm heart, I found that the master has praised my devotion and mind; even if it goes wrong in the telling, if it is good in the heart, Rama is pleased, knowing what is in his servant's heart.

first: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किये की। करत सुरति सय बार हिये की॥
en: The Lord does not keep in mind a fault once made, but remembers a hundred times the love in the heart. The very sin for which he killed Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later committed too,

first: सोइ करतूति बिभीषन केरी। सपनेहुँ सो न राम हिय हेरी॥
en: and Vibhishana did the same, yet Rama did not think of it even in a dream; instead he honoured them when meeting Bharat and praised them in the royal court.

first: दो॰ – प्रभु तरु तर कपि डार पर, ते किय आपु समान।
en: The Lord sat under the tree while the monkeys sat on the branches, yet he made them equal to himself; Tulsi says there is no master anywhere like Rama, a store of good nature.

first: राम निकाई रावरी, है सबही को नीक।
en: Rama, your goodness is good for everyone; if this is always true, then it will be good for Tulsi too.

first: एहि बिधि निज गुन दोष कहि, सबहि बहुरि सिर नाइ।
en: Having told my good and bad points in this way, and bowing my head again to all, I now tell the pure fame of Raghubar, which on hearing destroys the sins of the age.

first: चौ॰ – जागबलिक जो कथा सुहाई। भरद्वाज मुनिबरहि सुनाई॥
en: The lovely story that Yajnavalkya told to the great sage Bharadvaj, I will tell that dialogue in full; listen, all good people, with joy.

first: सम्भु कीन्ह यह चरित सुहावा। बहुरि कृपा करि उमहि सुनावा॥
en: Shambhu made this lovely story and then kindly told it to Uma; Shiva then gave it to Kakabhushundi, seeing him fit for devotion to Rama.

first: तेहि सन जागबलिक पुनि पावा। तिन्ह पुनि मरवाज प्रति गावा॥
en: From him Yajnavalkya received it, and he then sang it to Bharadvaj; both the hearer and the teller were alike in nature, saw all as equal, and knew Hari's play.

first: जानहिँ तीनि काल निज-ज्ञाना। करतल गत आमलक समाना।
en: By their knowledge they knew the past, present and future like a fruit held in the palm; and other wise devotees of Hari tell, hear and understand it in many ways.

first: दो॰ – मैं पुनि निज गुरुसन सुनी, कथा सो सूकरखेत।
en: Then I heard that story from my own Guru at Sukarkhet; but I was a child then, quite without understanding, and did not grasp it as it is.

first: सीता बकता ज्ञान-निधि, कथा राम के गूढ़।
en: Rama's story is deep, and both its hearer and teller should be stores of wisdom; how could I understand it, a dull being, seized by the sins of the age and very foolish?

first: चौ॰ – तदपिकही गुरुबारहि बारा। समुझि परी कछु भति अनुसारा।
en: Still, my Guru told it again and again, and I understood some of it as my mind allowed; that same story I will put into the common tongue, so that my own mind may be at peace.

first: जस कछु बुधि-बिबेक-बल मेरे। तस कहिहउँ हिय हरि के प्रेरे॥
en: With whatever strength of mind and judgment I have, I will tell it as Hari moves my heart; I tell this story, which removes my own doubt, delusion and error, and is a boat across the river of worldly life.

first: बुध-बिस्राम सकल-जन-रञ्जनि। राम-कथा कलि-कलुष-बिभञ्जनि॥
en: Rama's story gives rest to the wise, delights all people and destroys the sins of the age; Rama's story is a peahen to the serpent of the Kali age, and the firewood that kindles the fire of wisdom.

first: रामकथा कलि कामद गाई। सुजन सजीवनि मूरि सुहाई॥
en: Rama's story is said to be the wish-giving cow in the Kali age and a lovely life-giving herb for the good; it is a river of nectar on earth, destroyer of fear, and a snake that eats the frogs of error.

first: असुर सेन सम नरक निकन्दिनि। साधु बिधुध कुल हित गिरिनन्दिनि।
en: Like Parvati, it destroys the demon army of hell and does good to the family of saintly gods; it is like Lakshmi to the ocean of the saints, and like the steady earth that bears the whole world's weight.

first: जमगन मुँह मसि जग जमुना सी। जीवन मुकुति हेतु जनु कासी॥
en: Like the Yamuna, it blackens the faces of Yama's messengers; it is like Kashi, giving freedom in this life; it is dear to Rama like the holy tulsi, and to Tulsidas it is like his loving mother Hulsi.

first: सिव प्रिय मेकल सैल सुता सी। सकल सिद्धि सुख सम्पतिरासी।
en: It is dear to Shiva like the Narmada, daughter of Mount Mekal; it is a heap of all powers, joy and wealth; it is like Aditi, mother of the gods of good virtues, and the very height of love and devotion to Raghubar.

first: दो॰ – रामकथा मन्दाकिनी, चित्रकूट चित चारु।
en: Tulsi says Rama's story is the Mandakini river, a pure mind is lovely Chitrakut, and fine love is the forest where Sita and Raghubir roam.
